mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases risk aversion and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. The relationship is negative: higher UNRATE values predict negative returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an extremely accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and inflation is rising (CPIAUCSL > 210), it indicates a 'growth at risk' scenario where the Fed is forced to maintain low rates despite inflation, which increases equity risk premiums and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5 AND CPIAUCSL > 210, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In recessions marked by declining GDP (GDPC1 < 11500), a rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates a recovery in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when GDPC1 < 11500 AND HOUST > 450, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 212.5 indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 212.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above 100 and employment (PAYEMS) is above 133000, it indicates a strong labor market and improving economic conditions, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when INDPRO > 100 AND PAYEMS > 133000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In low-rate regimes (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), a rising Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures that may lead to monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days. The signal is activated when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% over the past month.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5 AND CPIAUCSL > 213.235, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) above 450,000 units indicates a strong housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when HOUST > 450, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.
